trial_title: Fludarabine in Treating Patients With Steroid-Resistant Chronic Graft- Versus-Host Disease
brief_summary:
RATIONALE: Fludarabine may be an effective treatment for graft-versus-host disease caused by bone marrow transplantation.

PURPOSE: Phase I/II trial to study the effectiveness of fludarabine in treating patients who have chronic graft-versus-host disease that has not responded to steroid therapy.

eligibility_table.criterion: Histologically or clinically proven chronic graft versus host disease (GVHD) that has failed to respond to at least 1 month of treatment with the following: Steroids (greater than 0.5 mg/kg/day) AND Cyclosporine or a cytotoxic agent (azathioprine or mercaptopurine) OR Other experimental treatment (such as chloroquine)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has systemic mastocytosis and does not have chronic graft versus host disease (GVHD), which is a specific requirement for this criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: All allogeneic bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplantation patients eligible regardless of underlying disease for which transplantation was performed if: At least 45 days since prior transplantation
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not undergone any allogeneic bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplantation, making her ineligible for this criterion.

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced no relapse of systemic mastocytosis as defined by a serum tryptase level ≤20 ng/mL in the past 6 months?
Has the patient maintained donor hematopoiesis with ≥50% donor chimerism in peripheral blood or bone marrow after treatment with fludarabine?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients with a rapid deterioration of GVHD that is considered life threatening if not controlled are eligible after receiving high dose steroids (greater than 1 mg/kg/day) for at least 10 days
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not have GVHD, and therefore does not meet the eligibility for rapid deterioration of GVHD requiring high dose steroids.

eligibility_table.criterion: Fertile patients must use effective contraception
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is female and of childbearing age, but there is no information provided about contraception use. However, assuming she is compliant, this criterion can be considered met.

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any concurrent cytotoxic drugs in the past 30 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: Concurrent steroids allowed but must be tapered to less than 0.5 mg/kg/day of prednisone or equivalent prior to starting study drug (if symptomatic flare develops during taper, patients may continue on the lowest dose thought to produce stabilization)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is currently on a steroid taper and is receiving 125 mg IV steroids, which exceeds the allowed dose of less than 0.5 mg/kg/day prior to starting the study drug.

eligibility_table.criterion: Concurrent cyclosporine and other nonmyelosuppressive drugs allowed
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently receiving cyclosporine or any other nonmyelosuppressive drugs alongside the steroid treatment?
Has the patient received any myelosuppressive agents, such as azathioprine or mercaptopurine, in the past 30 days?
